_description: Global sovereign AI / data-center compute initiatives, collected to estimate each country's sovereign DC workload (MW) and its share of the global total, using two independent triangulation signals: government-announced sovereign BUDGET (USD) and government-announced sovereign CAPACITY (MW or GPU count).

_methodology.scope_definition: A program counts as 'sovereign' only if a government body, sovereign wealth fund, or state-owned enterprise is the funder, co-funder, subsidizer, or explicit sponsor of domestic AI/data-center compute capacity for reasons of AI sovereignty. Ordinary private or hyperscaler commercial data-center investment (e.g. a standalone AWS/Google/Microsoft lease, or a pure private JV like the ~$500B global 'Stargate' OpenAI/Oracle/SoftBank vehicle) is explicitly EXCLUDED even when politically endorsed, unless government capital, subsidy, land, or equity is directly in the deal.
_methodology.two_independent_signals: Per country, two signals are collected independently, exactly as they were announced: (1) sovereign BUDGET announced by government (USD), and (2) sovereign CAPACITY announced (MW directly, or GPU/accelerator count). These often come from different programs/announcements within the same country and are not necessarily 1:1 linked -- e.g. Saudi Arabia's $100B HUMAIN commitment and its 6.6GW capacity target are both 'headline' figures for the same overall push but were not derived from each other.
_methodology.triangulation_rule: best_estimate_mw prefers, in order: (a) directly announced MW; (b) GPU/accelerator count converted via a kW/GPU factor; (c) budget converted via a $/MW capex benchmark, used only when neither (a) nor (b) is available. This avoids compounding two uncertain conversions.

conversion_benchmarks.note_gpu_factor: Includes server overhead + facility PUE (~1.3-1.4x), per SemiAnalysis / NVIDIA / TRG Datacenters benchmarks (2024-2026).
conversion_benchmarks.budget_to_mw_note: Real-world $/MW ranges $15-20M (shell/infra only) to $30-38M (all-in incl. GPUs, 2025-26 Blackwell-era). Budget-based MW estimates below use a midpoint appropriate to what the underlying budget appears to cover (grant/subsidy vs full capex) and should be read as an order-of-magnitude band, not a precise figure.

global_sanity_check.note: Bottom-up sovereign-specific total here (~$130-320B budget, ~5.6-18.6GW depending on scope) is a small fraction of these all-in global AI infrastructure figures, which are dominated by private hyperscaler capex (Stargate, Meta, Google, Microsoft, Amazon), not government-sovereign programs.

known_limitations: Government figures are frequently multi-year, blended public/private, or subsidy/loan (not pure capex) — comparability across countries is approximate.
GPU counts mix H100/H200/Blackwell generations; a single blended kW/GPU factor per country is a simplification.

Some 'sovereign' Gulf-state figures (UAE MGX, Qatar Qai/Brookfield, Kuwait KIA/Helix) are financial co-investment in JVs with foreign hyperscalers/asset managers and may not be fully sited domestically — flagged per-country as 'sovereignty_purity'.
EU-level money (EuroHPC AI Gigafactories, €20B) is not yet allocated to specific member states as of data collection — kept as a separate supranational line, not attributed to any one country.

Countries/programs with real budgets but no credible attributable compute-hardware share (e.g. Thailand's workforce/data-bank spending, Philippines' NAICRI) are listed for completeness with mw_best_estimate = null rather than force-fit an estimate.

summary.headline_takeaway: Japan's identified sovereign AI/DC commitments (~$7.1B budget, ~300MW) don't shift under a 2030 lens -- every Japanese program concludes at or before 2029. Saudi Arabia and Israel do shift: Saudi Arabia's 6.6GW/$100B is an explicit 2025-2035 decade plan (linear run-rate: ~3.3GW/$50B by 2030), and Israel's 100,000-GPU/$25-30B program is an explicit 2027-2032 window (linear run-rate: ~60,000 GPUs (~120MW)/~$15B by 2030). Since Japan's figure is fixed while the two largest 'far-future' commitments shrink under the 2030 lens, Japan's global share is slightly HIGHER by 2030 (~2.0% of MW) than on an all-time-horizon basis (~1.6%). Several Gulf-adjacent programs (UAE's Stargate campus, Qatar, Kuwait's Helix venture, the EU's pending Gigafactories) have no disclosed completion date at all -- their 'by 2030' figures are shown at full value but flagged UNCERTAIN, since real-world buildout could plausibly land short of that by 2030.

_sense_check_gdp.source: IMF World Economic Outlook, April 2026 edition (nominal GDP, current prices, USD) -- Taiwan and EU-27 figures sourced from secondary compilations (statisticstimes.com, whatisgdp.com) since IMF WEO does not tabulate them directly; population from World Population Review 2026 / Eurostat.
_sense_check_gdp.note: "EU supranational (unallocated)" is excluded from this table -- it is a specific EU-level compute program, not the whole EU-27 economy, so comparing its budget/MW share against the EU's ~18% GDP share would conflate scopes.
